Grepped merge_commit_msg.py before handing off, and the premise does not hold in that file. Nothing in it cuts a squash subject at 72 characters. I did not pin line numbers to a cut, because there is none to pin.

What the file does, in the plan-red-84cc5bc tree:
- merge_commit_msg.py:110-117 `subject_line` returns the squash subject as `f"{title} (#{pr})"` with no slicing.
- merge_commit_msg.py:124-144 `title_problem` checks only non-ASCII characters, a title that is just the branch name, and the Word(scope): summary shape. It has no length check.
- merge_commit_msg.py:61 `LINE_WIDTH = 110`. It is applied at 316-326 (`layout_problems`), and 320-321 reports an over-wide line as a problem.
- merge_commit_msg.py:329-337 `subject_problem` requires line 1 to equal `subject_line(...)` exactly. build (380-402) therefore refuses any other subject and truncates nothing.
- The only 72-character limits in the harness plugin are guidance text: reference/commit_format.md:60 and skills/c-msg/SKILL.md:100-102. That is the c-msg skill, not this script.

So the review observation is probably about somewhere else, such as GitHub's own rendering or the c-msg guidance, or the squash title was already cut upstream. A warning would need a new rule here, probably in `title_problem` (124-144) or in `layout_problems` (316-326). A line-pinned TODO would still describe a defect I could not reproduce.

There is also no `harness:add-todo` skill in this tree, so I could not confirm what `-r 3` means. The closest agent is `harness:todo-editor`.
